units.title: Free Will and Responsibility
units.sub: A programmed “I love you” is not love; love requires a real choice.

share.v: Choose today whom you will serve … but as for me and my house, we will serve Yahweh.

blocks.h: An engineer could design a robot that says “I love you” right on time every day. But no one would be moved by it, because it cannot choose not to say it.
Love is precious precisely because it could be withheld, yet is freely given. When God made human beings, he gave them the ability to choose.
I call heaven and earth to witness against you today that I have set before you life and death, the blessing and the curse. Therefore choose life, that you may live, you and your descendants.
Did the brain move first?

In 1983 the neuroscientist Benjamin Libet asked participants to flex their wrist whenever they felt like it and to note the position of a clock at the moment they “decided to move.” He found that brain activity called the “readiness potential” began several hundred milliseconds before the moment participants were aware of deciding. Many people concluded from this that free will is only an illusion.

A ship at sea is constantly pushed by wind and waves; that is real. Yet the helmsman is still at the wheel, setting the course. The brain’s mechanisms are like the wind and waves: real, but not necessarily replacing the one at the helm.

Things are not that simple. Libet himself believed that consciousness can still “veto” an impulse before the action. In 2012 Aaron Schurger and colleagues proposed a model in which the readiness potential may simply be the build-up of the brain’s spontaneous fluctuations, triggering the action only when it crosses a threshold, and does not mean that “the decision was already made.”

Moreover, these experiments study movements like “flick your hand whenever you like,” actions with no reason and no consequences. The truly important choices in life, such as whether to forgive or whether to keep a promise, often involve long reflection and struggle. The two are very different.
Before spontaneous movements, a readiness potential can be measured in the brain, and it appears before participants are aware of deciding.
Neuroscientists still debate whether the readiness potential represents a “decision” or a “build-up of random fluctuations.”

If humans had no choice at all, moral responsibility, genuine love and rational thought would all lose their meaning. Real human choice fits the teaching that humans are made in God’s image. C. S. Lewis argued that by giving humans free will God made evil possible, but also made possible the only kind of love worth having.
Perspectives Room

items.h: Every choice is determined by prior causes; freedom is only a feeling. Critics point out that this makes it hard to ground moral responsibility.
As long as an action comes from your own will and is not forced by outside pressure, it is free; freedom and causation can coexist. Many Reformed theologians hold a similar view.

In the very same situation, a person truly could have chosen otherwise. Many theologians in the Arminian tradition hold this view. Evangelicals differ on this question, but all affirm that people are accountable to God for their choices.

blocks.h: Love needs freedom; freedom is for love
God could have made a world where no one could go wrong, and no one could love. Instead he chose to make a world where people can say “no,” because he wanted children, not machines.
For you, brothers, were called for freedom. Only don’t use your freedom for gain to the flesh, but through love be servants to one another.
Our love is a response to God’s loving us first.
We love him, because he first loved us.
Think about it: what choice today could you use to express love for God and for others?
Reflect: Do I often blame my choices on circumstances, genes or other people, unwilling to take responsibility?

Prayer: Lord Jesus, thank you for giving me the freedom to choose. Today I choose once again to let you reign. May my freedom not become an excuse for indulgence, but a way to serve others in love. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Let Jesus reign: the best use of freedom is to freely hand the throne to Jesus.
Deny yourself: true freedom is not doing whatever you want, but being able to choose love and service.
Review and correction: take responsibility for your choices; when wrong, admit it, correct course and start again.

blocks.h: This week: pick one thing you have always blamed on other people or your circumstances, write down “one choice I can make,” and act on it this week.
Quiz

quiz.q: What did Libet’s experiment find?
o: The readiness potential appears several hundred milliseconds before the conscious decision
Humans have no freedom at all
The brain is not involved in making decisions
quiz.e: But what it means is still debated.

quiz.q: How did Schurger and colleagues explain the readiness potential?
o: It is a signal from the soul
It proves free will exists
It may simply be a build-up of the brain’s spontaneous fluctuations
quiz.e: This calls into question the claim that “the decision was already made.”

quiz.q: Why do we say love requires freedom?
o: Because freedom matters more than love
“Love” that is forced or programmed is not true love
Because God doesn’t care about human choices
quiz.e: Choosing to love when you could choose not to is what real love is.

units.title: Longing for Eternity
units.sub: Nothing in this world can fill the human heart, because the heart was made for eternity.

share.v: He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in their hearts, yet so that man can’t find out the work that God has done from the beginning even to the end.

blocks.h: You finally get something you have long hoped for, yet the happiness quickly fades. When you see a magnificent starry sky or hear moving music, an inexpressible longing wells up, as if you were homesick for a home you have never visited.
More than sixteen hundred years ago, Augustine opened his Confessions by telling God, in essence: you made us for yourself, and our heart is restless until it rests in you (paraphrased).
He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in their hearts, yet so that man can’t find out the work that God has done from the beginning even to the end.
Three longings of the human heart

items: Meaning: people want not only to live, but to know why they live.
Beauty: beautiful scenery, music and art move us, yet always leave a longing that says “this isn’t enough.”
Justice: when we see injustice, we long for the day when everything is set right.

blocks.h: The psychiatrist Viktor Frankl was imprisoned in Nazi concentration camps. In Man’s Search for Meaning he recorded that in the worst conditions, those who could find a meaning to live for were often better able to endure.

Babies get hungry because food exists; people get thirsty because water exists. If the human heart has a longing that nothing in this world can satisfy, perhaps that shows we were made for another world.

This is C. S. Lewis’s “argument from desire.” In Mere Christianity he wrote, in essence, that if I find in myself a desire that no experience in this world can satisfy, the most probable explanation is that I was made for another world.

Critics say that wanting something does not mean it exists; people want to fly, for example. Lewis distinguished “natural desires” (such as hunger and sleep, which have corresponding satisfactions) from “fanciful desires” (such as wanting to fly or wanting fairyland). He argued that the longing for eternity belongs to the first kind: it is universal, and nothing in all creation satisfies it. This is still a philosophical inference, not a proof.
Frankl survived the concentration camps; the German original of Man’s Search for Meaning was published in 1946.
The search for meaning affects a person’s ability to face suffering. This is the core claim of Frankl’s “logotherapy,” and it inspired later research in the psychology of meaning.
The human heart has a longing that created things cannot satisfy; the best explanation is that we were made for the eternal God. This is C. S. Lewis’s argument from desire.
Perspectives Room

items.h: The longing for eternity may be a by-product of evolution or psychology, a wish that humans project outward, which does not mean eternity really exists.
A longing that is universal, deep and never satisfied in this world looks more like something pointing to its true object. Ecclesiastes says it is God who set eternity in the human heart.

blocks.h: Pleasures forevermore in his presence
In Ecclesiastes, the Hebrew word here means “forever.” God placed a longing for eternity in the human heart so that we would not be content with temporary things, but would come and seek him.
You will show me the path of life. In your presence is fullness of joy. In your right hand there are pleasures forever more.
while we don’t look at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen. For the things which are seen are temporal, but the things which are not seen are eternal.
Who do I have in heaven? There is no one on earth who I desire besides you. My flesh and my heart fails, but God is the strength of my heart and my portion forever.
Recall a beautiful moment that made you think, “I want more.” Bring that longing before God and acknowledge that only he can satisfy it.
Reflect: What have I recently tried to use to fill the emptiness in my heart?

Prayer: Eternal God, you have set eternity in my heart. Forgive me for seeking satisfaction from temporary things. Let me find fullness of joy in your presence, and fix my eyes on the eternal things that cannot be seen. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: From the temporary to the eternal: measure today’s time, money and energy with eternity in view.
Let Jesus receive all the glory: every good thing is a signpost pointing to him; don’t mistake the signpost for the destination.
Give thanks in everything: thank God in every beautiful moment, and let enjoyment become worship.

blocks.h: This week: list three things you have recently poured the most energy into, and ask yourself: a hundred years from now, which of them will still matter? Adjust one, and give that time to eternal things.
Quiz

quiz.q: According to Ecclesiastes 3:11, what has God set in human hearts?
o: Wealth
Eternity (the Hebrew means “forever”)
Words of wisdom
quiz.e: “He has also set eternity in their hearts.” The Hebrew word means “forever.”

quiz.q: What is the main inference of C. S. Lewis’s argument from desire?
o: People want to fly, so people can fly
All longings are mere fantasy
A longing this world cannot satisfy suggests we were made for another world
quiz.e: This is a philosophical inference, not a strict proof.

quiz.q: What did Frankl observe in the concentration camps?
o: Those who found a meaning to live for were often better able to endure
Physical strength was the only factor
Meaning had nothing to do with survival
quiz.e: He later developed “logotherapy.”

units.title: Language: A Bridge Between Minds
units.sub: With a limited set of words we can say an unlimited range of things; this bridge links one heart to another.

share.v: The Word became flesh, and lived among us. We saw his glory, such glory as of the only born Son of the Father, full of grace and truth.

blocks.h: The sentence you are reading right now has very likely never been written in exactly this way before, yet you understand it at once.

A few dozen sounds and a few thousand words can produce an unlimited number of new sentences: about the past, the future, things never seen, love and truth. Through language, the meaning in one heart travels into another.

In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made through him. Without him, nothing was made that has been made.
What makes human language unique

items: Unlimited combinations: a limited set of words plus grammatical rules can build an unlimited number of sentences, nested layer upon layer.
Talking about what isn’t here: the past, the future, abstract justice and hope can all be put into words.
Everyone can learn it: the world has more than seven thousand languages, and every normally developing child learns the language around them within a few years.

blocks.h: LEGO bricks come in only a few dozen shapes, yet they can build an endless variety of creations. Language is the same: limited parts, unlimited creativity.

In the 1970s the psychologist Herbert Terrace taught a chimpanzee named “Nim” sign language. Nim learned many signs, but when the team carefully analyzed the videotapes, they found that most of his signs imitated his trainers, and he did not produce grammatically structured sentences.

In 2002 Marc Hauser, Noam Chomsky and Tecumseh Fitch proposed in Science that “recursion,” the ability to nest structures layer upon layer, may be the uniquely human core of language. Animals also communicate in rich ways, such as the honeybee’s dance and monkeys’ alarm calls, but there is currently no evidence that they have this kind of open-ended, infinitely combinable grammar. How language originated remains one of the hardest questions in science.
There are more than seven thousand living languages in the world.
Animals have rich communication systems, but trained apes have not shown the kind of grammatical, infinitely combinable language that humans have.
Scholars still debate how the human capacity for language originated and whether recursion is truly its uniquely human core.

The Bible says, “In the beginning was the Word”: God is a God who speaks and communicates. That humans can express meaning and build relationships through language is best explained by our being made in the image of this speaking God. This is a philosophical and theological inference.
In the beginning was the Word
The “Word” in John’s Gospel is the Greek logos, meaning both word and reason. God created all things through his word, and through his word he reveals himself to us.
God gave Adam the task of naming, and for the first time a human being used language to take part in God’s creation.

Out of the ground Yahweh God formed every animal of the field, and every bird of the sky, and brought them to the man to see what he would call them. Whatever the man called every living creature became its name.
Most wonderful of all, the Word himself became human and lived among us, so that we could know God.
The Word became flesh, and lived among us. We saw his glory, such glory as of the only born Son of the Father, full of grace and truth.
Read John 1:14 slowly. The Word who created language came in person among us to speak to us.
Reflect: Lately, have my words been building people up or tearing them down?
Prayer: Word made flesh, thank you for coming in person to speak to me. Cleanse my lips, so that my words carry grace and truth and become a blessing to others. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: The Bible is my standard: God speaks through his Word; read Scripture every day and let his words become my words.
920 (living out the ninefold fruit of the Spirit): let my words bear the Spirit’s fruit of love, kindness and gentleness.
Multiplication: language is a bridge between hearts; use it to pass the gospel on to the next person.

blocks.h: This week: every day this week, use one specific sentence to affirm or bless someone, such as a family member, a coworker, or a brother or sister in your fellowship.
Quiz

quiz.q: What is one of the most distinctive features of human language?
o: It is the loudest
It can only talk about what is present
A limited set of words can form unlimited sentences
quiz.e: Nested, unlimited combination is the hallmark of human language.

quiz.q: What did the study of Nim the chimpanzee find?
o: His signs were mostly imitation, and he did not produce grammatical sentences
He could write poetry
He learned English
quiz.e: Terrace’s team reached this conclusion after carefully analyzing the videotapes.

quiz.q: According to John 1:14, what did the Word become?
o: The law
Flesh
The temple
quiz.e: “The Word became flesh, and lived among us.”

units.title: Made for Love: Persons and Relationships
units.sub: We need relationships the way we need air, because the God who made us is himself a fellowship of love.

share.v: We love him, because he first loved us.

blocks.h: Since 1938, Harvard University has followed a group of people across their whole lives, one of the longest studies of adult development ever conducted. Its current director, Robert Waldinger, sums it up: one of the keys to health and happiness is warm, good relationships.
Not wealth, not fame, but having people who love you, and loving them in return.
Yahweh God said, “It is not good for the man to be alone. I will make him a helper comparable to him.”
Relationships are a human necessity

In 1958 the psychologist Harry Harlow gave baby monkeys a choice between two “surrogate mothers”: one made of wire and holding a milk bottle, the other covered in soft cloth with no milk. The baby monkeys spent most of their time clinging to the cloth mother, going to the wire mother only when hungry to drink.
A glowing coal left in the fire keeps burning hot; pull it out on its own and it soon goes cold. People are like that: cut off from loving relationships, the heart slowly grows cold.

The British psychiatrist John Bowlby proposed “attachment theory”: children need a stable emotional bond with their caregivers. Mary Ainsworth designed the “Strange Situation” procedure, observing how young children respond when separated from and reunited with a caregiver, and identified secure and insecure patterns of attachment.

A 2010 meta-analysis combining 148 studies and 308,849 participants found that people with stronger social relationships had about a 50% greater likelihood of survival over the follow-up period. This is correlational research and cannot directly prove cause and effect, but it shows that relationships and health are closely linked.
In Harlow’s experiments, baby monkeys preferred to cling to the cloth surrogate mother that offered contact comfort, not just to the one that provided food.
People with stronger social relationships have a higher likelihood of survival (an odds ratio of about 1.5 in the meta-analysis); this is a correlation, and the mechanisms are still being studied.
Early attachment patterns are linked to later relationships, but scholars still debate how large the effect is and whether it can change; attachment is not fixed for life.

Humans have a deep need for love and relationship, which fits the Bible’s revelation: we are made in the image of the triune God, and before creation there was already love among the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. This is a theological and philosophical inference.
The triune God: an eternal fellowship of love
God said, “Let’s make man in our image, after our likeness …”

God says “let us” make man in “our” image. Christians believe that the one God exists in three persons: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. Before the world was made, love was already flowing within God.
… for you loved me before the foundation of the world.
So “God is love” is not a slogan. A solitary god would need creatures in order to love; but the triune God has always been love from eternity. We long for love because we are made in his image.
God is love, and he who remains in love remains in God, and God remains in him.
Think of someone who once loved you unconditionally, and thank God for them. That love was a reflection of God’s love.
Reflect: Lately, have I treated tasks as more important than people, and things as more important than relationships?
Prayer: Triune God, you are love, and you made me in your image. Fill me with your love, so that I first draw near to you and can then sincerely love the people around me. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: The order of relationships: God → self → others → tasks. Draw near to God first, and then you can love others in a healthy way.
235 (three kinds of spiritual relationships): we need spiritual companions, spiritual parents and children, and comrades in arms; don’t walk the road of faith alone.
People matter more than tasks: in the middle of busyness, stop first and see the person.

blocks.h: This week: arrange to meet or call a friend or family member you haven’t been in touch with for a while, and give them your full attention, with your phone put away.
Quiz

quiz.q: In Harlow’s experiment, which surrogate mother did the baby monkeys cling to most of the time?
o: The wire mother with the milk bottle
The cloth mother
Neither
quiz.e: Contact comfort attracted the baby monkeys more than food.

quiz.q: What did the 2010 meta-analysis find social relationships to be associated with?
o: Income
Height
Likelihood of survival
quiz.e: People with stronger relationships had about a 50% higher likelihood of survival, but this is a correlation.

quiz.q: Why do we say the triune God “has always been love”?
o: Before creation there was love among the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit
Because God needed human company
Because humans invented love
quiz.e: “For you loved me before the foundation of the world.” (John 17:24)

units.title: Conscience and Grace
units.sub: Conscience tells us we have done wrong but cannot erase the past; only the cross can cleanse the conscience.

share.v: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

blocks.h: When you do something wrong, even if no one else knows, your heart is still uneasy. Late at night, when all is quiet, it comes back again and again.
Why do we feel this way? Why, even when we try to convince ourselves that “it’s fine,” does conscience refuse to be quiet?
because if our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart, and knows all things.
Guilt and shame

Research by the psychologist June Tangney and colleagues distinguishes two feelings: guilt focuses on “I did a bad thing” and often leads to apology and repair; shame focuses on “I am a bad person” and often makes people want to hide, deny or lash out.

Conscience is like a warning light on a car’s dashboard. Pulling out the bulb won’t fix the engine, and staring at the light while blaming yourself won’t fix the car either. What you need is a mechanic who can fix the engine.

Research also shows that healthy guilt is often linked to empathy and responsible behavior, while chronic shame is associated with more psychological distress. This resembles the Bible’s picture: God wants us to confess our actions, but not to be crushed by condemnation.

Psychology can help people deal with unhealthy shame, but there is one thing it cannot do: declare, “Your sins are forgiven.” Forgiveness can only be given by the one who was wronged. Deep down, our conscience knows that the one we have ultimately wronged is the God who wrote his law on our hearts.
Guilt (focused on behavior) more often leads to repair; shame (focused on the self) more often leads to avoidance and defensiveness.
Even without outside punishment, people feel uneasy when they violate their own moral standards; “moral emotions” such as guilt and shame have long been studied in psychology.

Conscience universally points to a moral Lawgiver and Judge, and also makes us long for someone who can forgive. The Christian faith proclaims that this Forgiver is Jesus, who bore our sins on the cross. This is a theological inference and proclamation.
The cross: where the conscience is cleansed
God is righteous and cannot treat sin as if it never happened; God is loving and does not want us crushed by sin. At the cross, righteousness and love meet.
But God commends his own love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without defect to God, cleanse your conscience from dead works to serve the living God?
“Come now, and let’s reason together,” says Yahweh: “Though your sins are as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow. Though they are red like crimson, they shall be as wool.”
So when our conscience accuses us, we don’t need to hide, and we don’t need to punish ourselves. We can come to the cross, confess, and receive complete forgiveness.
There is therefore now no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus, who don’t walk according to the flesh, but according to the Spirit.
Be still for a moment, and honestly bring before God the thing you least want anyone to know. He already knows, and he still loves you.
Reflect: Do I deal with guilt through denial, busyness or self-punishment, or do I come to the cross?

Prayer: Lord Jesus, thank you for shedding your blood and giving your life for me. I confess my sins; forgive me according to your promise and cleanse my conscience, so that I no longer live under condemnation but serve you in your grace. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
321 Life Application

items: Humility overcomes pride: confession is returning to our proper place, letting humans be human and letting God be God.
Selflessness (the self-emptied life): it is no longer I, but Christ living in me; those who have been forgiven learn to forgive others.
Become an overcomer: in Christ there is no condemnation; rely on the Holy Spirit every day to overcome the grip of sin.

blocks.h: This week: confess to God one thing you have been carrying in your heart; if you have wronged someone, take the initiative this week to apologize and make amends.

Congratulations on completing the Mind Hall! From consciousness, reason, morality and freedom to longing, language, relationships and conscience, you have seen a God who gives us minds, writes his law on our hearts, and came in person to cleanse our consciences.
Quiz

quiz.q: What is the main difference between guilt and shame?
o: Guilt focuses on behavior; shame focuses on the self
They are exactly the same
Shame is always better
quiz.e: Guilt says “I did wrong”; shame says “I am bad.”

quiz.q: According to Hebrews 9:14, what can cleanse our conscience?
o: Our own efforts
Time
The blood of Christ
quiz.e: “How much more will the blood of Christ … cleanse your conscience from dead works.”

quiz.q: According to 1 John 1:9, if we confess our sins, what will God do?
o: Ignore them
Forgive us our sins and cleanse us from all unrighteousness
Require us to make up for them before forgiving
quiz.e: Because God is faithful and righteous.

units.title: Memory and Forgetting
units.sub: We rewrite even yesterday’s events, but there is One who never forgets you.

share.v: Praise Yahweh, my soul, and don’t forget all his benefits,

blocks.h: On September 1, 1953, a 27-year-old American underwent brain surgery to control severe epilepsy. The seizures lessened, but from then on he could hardly form any new memories: a doctor who had just finished talking with him, stepped out and came back in, was a stranger to him again. He lived another 55 years.

Stranger still, he practiced tracing a star while looking in a mirror over several days, and got better each day, yet every time he said he had never done it. His hand remembered, but “he” did not. What is the relationship between who you are and what you remember?
“Can a woman forget her nursing child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? Yes, these may forget, yet I will not forget you!
One operation rewrote the science of memory

The young man was Henry Molaison, referred to in the scientific literature during his lifetime only as H.M. The surgeon, William Scoville, removed tissue from the medial temporal lobes on both sides, including the front part of the hippocampus. In 1957 Scoville and the psychologist Brenda Milner published a report: his intelligence and short-term attention were largely intact, but he had lost the ability to form new long-term memories.

From this scientists learned that memory is not one big warehouse but several systems: the system that remembers “what happened” relies heavily on the hippocampus, while the system that learns a motor skill takes another route.

Memory is more like a veteran cook making a home-style dish again from leftovers than like a video recorder when you press play. Each time it comes to the table it is “that dish,” but the ingredients and the heat may differ from the last time.
Recall is also a kind of reconstruction

In 1974 Elizabeth Loftus and John Palmer had students watch films of car accidents and then asked about the speed. The group whose question used the word “smashed” estimated an average of 40.8 miles per hour; the group asked with “contacted” gave only 31.8. A week later, 32% of those asked with “smashed” said they had seen broken glass, though there was none in the film.

A survey commissioned by Taiwan’s Ministry of Health and Welfare (2020–2023) shows that the prevalence of dementia among people aged 65 and over is about 7.99%, and reaches 23.23% among those aged 85 and over. The World Health Organization estimates that in 2021 about 57 million people worldwide were living with dementia, with nearly 10 million new cases each year. This is very likely your family’s matter, not only someone else’s.

A 2015 study published in Brain combined brain imaging of young adults with biomarkers from a separate group of Alzheimer’s patients and inferred that the brain regions that long-term musical memory depends on are relatively less eroded by the disease. This may help explain why some elders cannot name their children yet can still sing along to old songs. This is an inference, and not every patient is like this.

The 2024 Lancet Commission estimated that if 14 risk factors, including hearing loss, high blood pressure, physical inactivity and social isolation, were completely eliminated, future cases of dementia might be reduced by about 45%. This is a population-level estimate. It does not mean that patients fell ill because they failed to take care of themselves.

Research on false memories is also contested. In the 1995 “lost in the mall” experiment about 25% of participants were judged to have formed a false memory, and a preregistered replication in 2023 (123 participants) found 35%. After re-examining the data, Chris Brewin and Bernice Andrews pointed out that only 14% of them clearly said they remembered it, so the number of true false memories is far smaller. Memory can be distorted, but implanting a whole event out of nothing is not so easy; and the memories of trauma survivors should not be dismissed lightly on this basis.
Memory research is moving fast, so we will look at it in layers.

After his surgery H.M. could not form new long-term memories of events, yet could still learn new motor skills. This established the key role of the hippocampal region and also shows that memory is not a single system.
Recall is easily influenced by information received afterward. The wording of a question alone is enough to change people’s estimates and descriptions of a car accident.
Dementia is one of the world’s leading causes of death and disability: the World Health Organization ranks it as the fifth leading cause of death, and about 57 million people were affected in 2021.
About four and a half out of ten future dementia cases “may” be preventable by reducing risk factors. The direction is widely taken seriously, but the exact proportion is still a modeled estimate.
How easily a complete false memory can be implanted is still debated in the field; why musical memory is better preserved is also still being studied.

In the end a person’s identity and worth do not depend on how much he himself remembers, but on God remembering him. This is a theological confession, not a conclusion of brain science. The theologian John Swinton’s Dementia: Living in the Memories of God starts from here, and he is also a trained psychiatric nurse and chaplain.
The viewpoints room
Is a person with dementia still “the same person”? This is a question many family members are afraid to say out loud.

items.h: A tradition going back to the philosopher John Locke holds that personal identity depends mainly on memory and psychological continuity. Its strength is that it fits our intuition: without the past, what is left of “me”?

Many caregivers and scholars point out that people also live in their bodies, habits, emotions and in other people’s memories; preferences, responses to music and reactions to gentleness often remain. Christians go further and hold that a person’s identity is finally kept by God’s knowing.

blocks.h: God’s “remembering” is the kind that acts

In the Bible, God’s “remembering” is often joined to action, which is not quite the same as a person recalling a past event. In the flood He remembered Noah, and the waters receded; when His enslaved people groaned, He remembered the covenant He had made, and the exodus began.
God remembered Noah, all the animals, and all the livestock that were with him in the ship; and God made a wind to pass over the earth. The waters subsided.
The all-knowing God also has things He chooses “not to remember.” This is the most relieving forgetting in the whole Bible.
I, even I, am he who blots out your transgressions for my own sake; and I will not remember your sins.

This forgiveness came at a cost. On the night He was betrayed, the Lord Jesus took bread and asked us to “remember” Him; the next day, on the cross, a robber who had nothing to offer asked just one thing, “remember me,” and received a promise. If being saved depended on my reciting the creeds word for word, a saint with dementia would be in danger; but what holds us is the hand of Christ.
He said to Jesus, “Lord, remember me when you come into your Kingdom.” Jesus said to him, “Assuredly I tell you, today you will be with me in Paradise.”
Open the photo album on your phone and find a picture from ten years ago. Recall the difficulties of that time, then count one thing God later carried you through, and say it out loud.
Meditate: what do I fear most being forgotten? Is there a sin that God no longer remembers, yet I still bring it out every day to condemn myself?

Pray: Faithful Lord, my memory will blur and my brain will age, but You have engraved me on the palms of Your hands. Forgive me for forgetting Your grace, and make me patient to love those who are slowly forgetting. If one day I do not even remember myself, hold me still. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: Letting God be God and people be people: declining memory is the limitation of being a creature. It is no shame, and it does not mean weak faith. We place our security in God’s faithfulness.
People matter more than tasks: an elder with dementia can no longer “do” anything, yet his dignity has not shrunk by an inch. Accompanying him is honoring the image of God.
920: caregivers are often exhausted. In this most wearing of relationships, living out selflessness includes speaking up to ask for help, and letting the church and professionals share the load.

blocks.h: This week: count your blessings: write down three things God carried you through and tell one family member. If you or a family member are showing continuing memory decline, please get an early evaluation from a neurologist or psychiatrist; this unit is not medical advice. Visit an elder, or phone a caregiver and ask how he is doing himself lately.
Pass it on: Is there a memory you would very much like never to forget? If one day you really forgot it, would you still be you?
Quiz

quiz.q: What does H.M.’s condition after his surgery best illustrate?
o: Memory is more than one system, and memory for events depends heavily on the hippocampus
The surgery left him completely unable to learn
All of a person’s intelligence is located in the hippocampus
quiz.e: He could not retain new events, yet could learn motor skills such as tracing a star.

quiz.q: What is the more balanced conclusion from the discussion around the 2023 “lost in the mall” replication?
o: False memories do not exist at all
Memory can be distorted, but how easily a whole event can be implanted is still debated
No one’s traumatic memories can be trusted
quiz.e: The reanalysis found that fewer people clearly remembered the invented event than originally reported; the memories of trauma survivors must not be dismissed lightly.

quiz.q: In Isaiah 43:25, what does God say He will not remember?
o: Our good deeds
Our names
Our sins
quiz.e: The all-knowing God blots out transgressions for His own sake; this forgiveness is fulfilled at the cross of Christ.

units.title: Why Do People Believe in God?
units.sub: If the brain is naturally inclined to believe in God, does that overturn faith, or is it a clue?

share.v: that they should seek the Lord, if perhaps they might reach out for him and find him, though he is not far from each one of us.

blocks.h: You are walking through a patch of tall grass at night, and something rustles. Your heart rate has already gone up, and your brain has not yet decided whether it is the wind or a snake.

Some scholars say that the human tendency to believe in God comes from right here: better to mistake the sound of wind for someone there than to miss a real danger. If that is true, has faith been explained away? You may not expect it, but even scholars in this field do not agree on the answer.
He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in their hearts, yet so that man can’t find out the work that God has done from the beginning even to the end.
A science of “believing”

The cognitive science of religion took shape gradually from the 1990s, and the name “cognitive science of religion” was proposed by Justin Barrett in 2000. The question it asks is very concrete: why do people all over the world, in every age, so commonly believe in beings beyond the human who act with intention?

Representative works include Pascal Boyer’s Religion Explained (2001), Scott Atran’s In Gods We Trust (2002) and Barrett’s Why Would Anyone Believe in God? (2004). These scholars do not share one position: Boyer and Atran explain religion from a naturalistic standpoint, while Barrett himself is a Christian.
The by-product hypothesis and the “hyperactive agency detector”

The mainstream view holds that religious belief may be a by-product of some everyday cognitive abilities: we guess at other people’s minds, we look for purpose in events, and we quickly sense that “someone seems to be there.” Barrett proposed the hypersensitive agency detection device (HADD): missing a real predator costs too much, while a false alarm is only a scare, so the detector leans toward being sensitive.

The smoke alarm at home is sometimes set off by toast, because the manufacturer would rather have it sound a few extra times than miss a real fire. The HADD hypothesis says that the brain may also carry an alarm like that, set on the sensitive side.
The evidence is not as firm as first thought

The hypothesis is attractive, but the experimental evidence is not solid. A 2022 review by Michiel van Elk concluded that the evidence for agency detection is mixed, that the link between mentalizing and supernatural belief has small effect sizes, and that cultural transmission (such as parents’ displays of faith) looks more central than innate tendencies; once belief has formed, it may also reinforce these tendencies in turn.

A 2017 study covering more than 67,000 people in the Netherlands, Switzerland and the United States found that empathy and autism-trait scores were not consistent predictors across countries; what had a large influence was seeing people around you genuinely live out their faith while growing up, which scholars call “credibility-enhancing displays.”
So the field currently has two main threads: cognitive tendencies, and cultural and family transmission. The relative weight of the two is still under discussion.
The genetic fallacy, and its limits

How a belief arose and whether it is true are two different questions. Treating the first as the answer to the second is called, in logic, the genetic fallacy. You may believe the earth goes around the sun only because you needed to pass an exam, and the earth goes around the sun all the same.

To be fair, the skeptic’s version can be made stronger: if a cognitive mechanism would produce belief whether or not God exists, then a belief produced by that mechanism alone carries little evidential weight. This argument deserves a serious reply, and cannot be dismissed with the two words “genetic fallacy.”

The philosopher Alvin Plantinga’s reply is that if God exists, He would quite likely make Himself known through just such tendencies of the mind (following Calvin’s “sense of the divine”); so whether the belief is reliable depends on whether God exists, which cognitive science cannot answer by itself. Barrett and Ian Church also argue that these findings are not enough to reassure atheists. Atheist philosophers mostly regard this as circular reasoning.
Let us separate fact, interpretation and inference.

People all over the world and in every age commonly tend to believe in beings with superhuman intentions. This is the phenomenon the cognitive science of religion seeks to explain; at the same time, many people do not believe.
The by-product hypothesis, that religious belief may be a by-product of everyday cognitive abilities, is the mainstream approach in this field, and other models still compete with it.
The claim that “hyperactive agency detection is the root of faith” has thin evidence. Many studies found weak or inconsistent results, and a 2022 review judged the relevant evidence to be mixed.

In a cross-national study of more than 67,000 people, seeing people around you genuinely live out their faith while growing up had a strong influence on supernatural belief. This is correlational data, and the direction of causation and the relative weight still need more research.

These studies cannot by themselves decide whether God exists: explaining the process of believing does not explain whether the object of belief exists. A theist can see the tendency as God’s preparation, and an atheist can see it as an evolutionary by-product. Both are inferences that go beyond the scientific data.
The viewpoints room
The same data, read several serious ways.

items.h: The tendency to believe in God comes from cognitive mechanisms and cultural transmission, neither of which requires God to exist. The great differences among the gods believed in by different cultures also fit this explanation. This is the position of many in academia today.

If God exists, it is entirely reasonable that He would give people, through natural processes, a tendency to seek Him, just as the fact that vision evolved does not mean the world in front of us is false. The weakness of this view is that it presupposes the very conclusion under dispute, so other evidence is still needed.

More important than an innate detector are the examples set by family and community. Believers and non-believers can both accept this finding, and it passes no judgment on whether faith is true or false.

blocks.h: He placed the seeking inside people

The Bible never presents people’s search for God as a human achievement. Ecclesiastes says He set eternity in human hearts, and Paul tells the philosophers of Athens that this very search is part of God’s arrangement.

He made from one blood every nation of men to dwell on all the surface of the earth, having determined appointed seasons and the boundaries of their dwellings, that they should seek the Lord, if perhaps they might reach out for him and find him, though he is not far from each one of us.

“Reach out for him” is honest language: it is the motion of groping in the dark. There was even an altar in Athens inscribed “To an unknown god.” A cognitive tendency can take a person only this far: the sense that someone ought to be there. As to who He is and what His attitude toward me is, an inner tendency alone cannot get us there.

because that which is known of God is revealed in them, for God revealed it to them. For the invisible things of him since the creation of the world are clearly seen, being perceived through the things that are made, even his everlasting power and divinity, that they may be without excuse.

So Paul did not stop at religious feeling. He led the Athenians to something that happened in history and can be investigated: Jesus rose from the dead. The center of faith therefore moves from “what my brain tends to believe” to “what happened on that morning two thousand years ago.”
because he has appointed a day in which he will judge the world in righteousness by the man whom he has ordained; of which he has given assurance to all men, in that he has raised him from the dead.
And there is a deeper layer still: it is not only that people seek God. The cross tells us that God came looking for people first.
We love him, because he first loved us.

Recall the earliest moment when you felt curious about God or about eternity. Perhaps it was gazing at the stars as a child, or the night a loved one died. Write down the question that was in your heart then.
Meditate: in whose life did I see faith? If someone looked for faith in me, what would they see?

Pray: Lord, thank You that while I did not yet know You, You had already placed a seeking in my heart. Help me to know You with an honest mind and a soft heart, and thank You that through the cross and resurrection of the Lord Jesus You came looking for me first. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: The Bible is my standard: the tendencies in the heart can lead a person to seek, but discerning the direction depends on God’s word. My feelings are not the final basis of faith.
Life first, then relationship, then ministry: research shows that seeing faith genuinely lived out has a great influence. My most powerful witness to my family is how I live each day.
Letting God be God and people be people: I do not need to win every debate. How the other person responds is between him and God; I am responsible only for honesty and respect.

blocks.h: This week: tell someone who has believed longer than you (or your child) one thing: in whose life did you first feel that faith might be true?
Pass it on: Do you think religion exists almost everywhere because our brains are prone to overthinking, or because we really are looking for something? What do you think yourself?
Quiz

quiz.q: What is the basic idea of the “hyperactive agency detection” hypothesis?
o: The human brain has a dedicated region for believing in God
Missing a real danger costs more than a false alarm, so the detector leans toward being sensitive
Only children have this tendency
quiz.e: This is Barrett’s view. Later research gives inconsistent evidence on whether it explains the root of faith.

quiz.q: In the 2017 cross-national study of more than 67,000 people, what had a strong influence on supernatural belief?
o: Seeing people around you genuinely live out their faith while growing up
How high one’s IQ is
The latitude of where one lives
quiz.e: Scholars call this credibility-enhancing displays. It reminds us that the transmission of faith is closely tied to the example of lives.

quiz.q: Which statement about the cognitive science of religion and the existence of God is most accurate?
o: It proves that God exists
It proves that God does not exist
It studies how people form beliefs, and by itself cannot decide whether God exists
quiz.e: Explaining the process of believing is not the same as answering whether the object of belief exists. The conclusions of both sides are further philosophical inferences.

units.title: AI and the Image of God
units.sub: When a machine can talk more like a person than a person does, where should human dignity rest?

share.v: God created man in his own image. In God’s image he created him; male and female he created them.

blocks.h: In a 2025 experiment, participants chatted by typing for five minutes with a real person and an AI at the same time, and then judged which one was the human. GPT-4.5, given a particular persona, was judged to be the human 73% of the time, higher than the real people.
In other words, in this test the humans lost to the machine. So what makes a person a person?
what is man, that you think of him? What is the son of man, that you care for him?
What it is doing: predicting the next word

At the core of a large language model is the statistical regularity, learned from huge amounts of text, of how words follow one another. The researcher Murray Shanahan describes its basic task this way: what word is most likely to come next? It then generates, one word at a time, a statistically likely continuation.

Imagine someone who has read every book in the library. The moment you start speaking, he can pick up where you left off, quickly and beautifully. The question is: does he continue so well because he understands you, or because he has read so much? That is exactly where the debate lies.

This also explains why it can say something wrong with a perfectly straight face. A statistically likely sentence is not necessarily a true sentence. So the book titles, Bible verses and quotations that AI generates must all be checked against the original source.
The Turing test and the Chinese room

In 1950 Alan Turing proposed the “imitation game”: a judge converses by text with a person and a machine, and if the judge cannot tell them apart, the machine passes. He wanted a testable procedure to replace the hard-to-define question “can machines think?”

In 2025 Cameron Jones and Benjamin Bergen tested this in a preregistered three-party experiment: GPT-4.5 73%, LLaMa-3.1-405B 56%, GPT-4o 21%, and the old chatbot ELIZA 23%. Without a persona prompt, GPT-4.5 dropped to 36%; GPT-4o and ELIZA were both run without persona prompts. This is a preprint, and the authors themselves say that it measures how humanlike the AI seems and is not a direct test of intelligence.

In 1980 the philosopher John Searle proposed the Chinese room: a person who does not understand Chinese processes characters by following a rule book, and those outside think someone inside understands Chinese. He argued that manipulating symbols is not by itself enough to produce understanding. Critics reply that understanding may belong to the whole system and need not reside in that one person. The debate has heated up again because of large language models.
Is it conscious? The honest answer

In 2023 a report by nineteen scholars, including Patrick Butlin and Robert Long, listed indicators drawn from existing theories of consciousness and evaluated AI against them. Its conclusion was that none of the AI systems of the time were conscious, but that there was also no evident technical barrier to building systems that satisfy those indicators. The theories of consciousness themselves are not settled (see the unit “The Mystery of Consciousness” in this hall), and at present no one can give a final answer to this question.
Real harm has already happened

Bias: in 2018 Joy Buolamwini and Timnit Gebru tested three commercial gender-classification systems. The error rate for darker-skinned women reached as high as 34.7%, while for lighter-skinned men it was at most 0.8%. What the systems learn is often a tilt already present in the training data.

Deepfakes: in a case made public in 2024, a finance employee in the Hong Kong office of the engineering firm Arup saw the “chief financial officer” and colleagues in a video conference who were all deepfake images, and sent out about HK$200 million (about US$25 million) in 15 transfers.

The church has begun to respond as well. In 2019 the Ethics & Religious Liberty Commission of the Southern Baptist Convention issued an evangelical statement of principles on AI, and the Catholic Church’s 2025 document Antiqua et Nova cautions that although AI has its uses, treating it as a substitute for God is idolatry. Both documents stress human dignity and responsibility.
Let us distinguish what is known, what is debated and what is an inference of faith.
Large language models learn the statistical regularities of large amounts of text and generate likely continuations of words. They may produce content that sounds plausible but is wrong.

In a preregistered experiment in 2025, GPT-4.5 with a particular persona was judged to be human 73% of the time in five-minute conversations. This preprint shows imitation ability, which is not the same as understanding or consciousness.

Whether AI has understanding or consciousness is not settled. A 2023 cross-disciplinary report concluded that the systems of the time were not conscious, while also saying there was no evident technical barrier; the Chinese room debate also continues.
Commercial systems have shown significant bias; deepfakes have been used in real, major fraud cases.

Human dignity comes from the image of God, not from computing power. This is a theological claim, and it does not change with how capable AI becomes: even if one day machines surpass people at everything, people would not lose their worth because of it. The dignity of a baby who cannot speak and of an elder with dementia is just as complete.
The viewpoints room
Several serious positions on AI.

items.h: Mind is a matter of function and organization. If a system shows comparable cognition and behavior, there is no principled reason to deny that it can have a mind. This is the position of many cognitive scientists and AI researchers.
Mind arises from biological processes, and a program, however ingenious, is only a simulation. Searle’s reasons are philosophical, and he is not defending a religious position.

items.n: The Christian view of the human person
items.h: Human dignity lies in God’s creation and calling, and does not depend on ability tests. Christians differ on whether a machine can be conscious, and this does not affect human dignity.

blocks.h: The image is an identity, not a grade
When Genesis first speaks of human beings, it says nothing about IQ, language or computing ability.
God created man in his own image. In God’s image he created him; male and female he created them.

Theologians differ on what the image of God includes. Common answers are rational and moral capacity, representing God in ruling over creation, and relationship with God and with others. Whichever account we take, it is an identity God has given to people, and no one has to win it back by passing an exam.
A tower that can be built very high may also cover over this identity. The problem at Babel was not the bricks or the technology, but the motives of the builders.
They said, “Come, let’s build ourselves a city, and a tower whose top reaches to the sky, and let’s make a name for ourselves, lest we be scattered abroad on the surface of the whole earth.”

The true image was fully displayed in one Person. He did not defeat people with computing power. He entered human weakness, gave His life for people on the cross, and rose from the dead. A machine can imitate sentences of comfort, but it has no scars from suffering for you.
He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation.
For we don’t have a high priest who can’t be touched with the feeling of our infirmities, but one who has been in all points tempted like we are, yet without sin.
When you use your phone or computer today, stop once and look at one real person near you: a family member, a shop clerk, a coworker. Say in your heart: this person bears the image of God.
Meditate: lately, have I treated people as tools and tools as my support? Is my sense of worth built on efficiency, or on God’s love?

Pray: Lord who made me, thank You for making me in Your image; my worth does not depend on my performance. Give me wisdom to use tools without worshiping them or fearing them. Thank You, Lord Jesus, for giving Your life for me, so that I could know You anew. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: People matter more than tasks, and relationships more than things: AI can save me time, and the time saved belongs to the person in front of me.
The Holy Spirit is my guide: AI can help me organize information, and the AI assistant in this app included, they are only tools. Prayer, repentance and praying for one another cannot be outsourced.
The Bible is my standard: every verse and claim AI gives me must be checked against the Bible itself. Test all things; hold firmly to what is good.

blocks.h: This week: agree on a deepfake-proof “family code word” with your family; if a call or video call asks you to transfer money, verify through a different channel first. Then phone an elder and greet them in your own voice.
Pass it on: If one day AI were better than people at everything, what do you think would remain of a person’s worth?
Quiz

quiz.q: Why might a large language model say something wrong with a perfectly straight face?
o: It lies on purpose
It generates statistically likely continuations, which does not guarantee the content is true
Its internet connection dropped
quiz.e: Statistically likely is not the same as factually correct. So information AI provides must be checked against the original source.

quiz.q: What was Searle’s Chinese room meant to argue?
o: Computers can never learn Chinese grammar
Chinese is harder than English
Manipulating symbols is not by itself enough to produce understanding
quiz.e: This is his claim. Critics respond that “the whole system may understand” and the like, and the discussion is still going on.

quiz.q: Where does the Christian faith say human dignity comes from?
o: The image of God
Ability that surpasses machines
Education and productivity
quiz.e: The dignity of a baby and of an elder with dementia is equally complete. It is an identity, not a grade.

units.title: Happiness and Meaning
units.sub: A study that has followed people for more than eighty years and a sermon preached on a mountainside two thousand years ago say strikingly similar things.

share.v: I have spoken these things to you, that my joy may remain in you, and that your joy may be made full.

blocks.h: In 1938 researchers began to follow 724 men: one group were Harvard sophomores, the other were boys from the poorest neighborhoods in Boston. They kept asking these men questions as they grew old, and then asked their children too.
In decades of data, the people who were most satisfied with their relationships at age fifty were the healthiest at eighty. What predicts old age is not cholesterol alone.
Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven. Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.
The quality of relationships

The Harvard Study of Adult Development began in 1938 with 724 men as the original participants, and later included their children. Its fourth director, Robert Waldinger, sums it up this way: good relationships make people happier and healthier, and what matters more than the number of friends is the quality of close relationships.

A related study asked 47 elderly couples to record their feelings for eight consecutive evenings: in couples with high marital satisfaction, happiness did not drop noticeably on days when their health got worse. This is a small sample, and the conclusion must not be used to blame anyone whose marriage or health has not gone well.
Relationships are like the shock absorbers in a car. On a smooth road you do not feel them, but when you hit a pothole you find out how much difference it makes whether you have them.
The original participants in this study were all men, and all American; what it shows is a long-term correlation, and it cannot be said directly that relationships “cause” long life.
Can money buy happiness?

In 1974 the economist Richard Easterlin pointed out that when people are compared at the same point in time, the rich are happier; but over the long run, as incomes in the United States rose, average happiness did not rise with them. This is called the Easterlin paradox.

The debate has not died down. In 2008 Betsey Stevenson and Justin Wolfers argued that income and happiness do have a positive long-term relationship; Easterlin replied that their data covered too short a period. In 2023 Matthew Killingsworth, Daniel Kahneman and Barbara Mellers collaborated on a reanalysis and found that among the least happy people, well-being levels off once income passes a certain level, while among everyone else it keeps rising.
A fair conclusion is this: poverty is real suffering, and money does help; but money cannot solve every problem, and it cannot replace meaning.
The treadmill and the World Happiness Report

In 1971 Philip Brickman and Donald Campbell proposed the “hedonic treadmill”: people gradually adapt to changes for better or worse. Later research revised this: the baseline differs from person to person and can also change, and severe, long-term disability may have lasting effects. So we must never tell a suffering person, “You’ll get used to it after a while.” The frequently cited 1978 study compared only 22 lottery winners with 29 accident victims with paraplegia or quadriplegia, a very small sample.

In the 2026 World Happiness Report, Finland ranked first for the ninth year in a row, and Costa Rica rose to fourth. The report also notes that average happiness among under-25s in the United States, Canada, Australia and New Zealand has fallen by 0.86 points compared with 2006–2010 (on a 0–10 scale), and several chapters explore the influence of social media; that debate is still going on.
Talking about meaning in the darkest place

The psychiatrist Viktor Frankl was imprisoned in Nazi concentration camps from 1942, and his parents, wife and brother all died in that catastrophe. In 1946 he dictated, over nine days, the book later translated as Man’s Search for Meaning, arguing that even in extreme circumstances people can still choose their attitude, and that meaning can sustain a person more than happiness can. Some scholars criticize this account for possibly implying that those who died had given up; he himself knew very well that survival was often a matter of chance. So this book can be used only to encourage oneself, never to measure others.
Faith and physical and mental health

Tyler VanderWeele and colleagues analyzed data on about 89,000 American women nurses and found that the suicide rate among those who attended religious services weekly was about one fifth that of those who never attended (based on only 36 cases, in a limited study population). The Global Flourishing Study published in 2025 (more than 200,000 people in 23 countries and territories) also reported that attending religious services is associated with flourishing in many areas. These are correlational studies. They cannot prove that faith is true, and they must not be turned around to blame any family that is suffering or has lost a loved one.
Let us take each claim separately and mark how certain it is.
The Harvard Study of Adult Development began following 724 men in 1938 and has extended to their children.
Good relationship quality is associated with better health and happiness in later life. The finding is consistent, but the original sample was limited and the data are correlational.

The long-term relationship between income and happiness is still debated: the Easterlin paradox and its critics each have data, and the 2023 collaborative study dealt with the relationship between income and everyday emotions.

Attending religious services is associated with lower suicide rates and with several measures of flourishing. The studies are not small, but the direction of causation and confounding factors still call for caution, and no one may be judged on this basis.
Human happiness cannot satisfy people because people were made for God. This is a faith interpretation, which happiness research can neither prove nor refute.
The viewpoints room
What is happiness? Several serious answers.

items.h: Happiness is simply feeling good and being satisfied with life. This is the easiest to measure and is the basis of most surveys. Critics say a person may also be content with a bad life.

A tradition going back to Aristotle holds that a good life consists in cultivating virtue and committing oneself to worthwhile things. Many atheists also live deeply and meaningfully without needing religion.

A person’s blessedness lies in a relationship with God, and there can be blessing even in mourning. Christians do not deny the joy and goodness of others; and this is no guarantee of an easy life, since believers may suffer too.

blocks.h: He says “blessed” in unexpected places

Jesus stood on the mountainside and placed the word “blessed” on the poor in spirit, those who mourn, and those who hunger and thirst for righteousness. This list looks like no happiness ranking, and it promises no one riches.
Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy. Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God. Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.
The author of Ecclesiastes tried everything, and his conclusion is surprisingly modern: a lifetime spent running on a treadmill.
behold, all was vanity and a chasing after wind, and there was no profit under the sun.
When Paul talked about contentment, he was in prison. The secret he spoke of was not positive thinking but a Presence.

I know how to be humbled, and I also know how to abound. In any and all circumstances I have learned the secret both to be filled and to be hungry, both to abound and to be in need. I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.

When Jesus spoke of “my joy,” it was on the night He was betrayed, before He went to the cross. This joy passed through the cross and came back to life from the empty tomb. That is why it can bear the worst news life has.
looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising its shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
Write down the names of three people who held you up when times were hard. Then say one word of thanks for each: first to God, and then, to one of them, in person or by message.
Meditate: of the things I have pursued lately, how long did satisfaction last once I got them? How much of my joy is built on things that cannot be taken away?

Pray: Lord Jesus, Your joy passed through the cross, so I do not have to pretend to be happy. When I have plenty, teach me gratitude; when I am in need and in mourning, be with me. Teach me to love others as You have loved me. In Jesus’ name, amen.
321 Life Application

items: Relationships matter more than things: take out this month’s schedule and see where the people closest to you appear in it.
Move from a temporary perspective to an eternal one: wealth is not the enemy, but it must not be the master. A person’s life does not consist of the abundance of his possessions.
920: every relationship is a place to practice selflessness. Joy is the fruit of the Spirit, and it grows on the road of loving others.

blocks.h: This week: invite someone to a meal with no phones, and ask: “What has really been wearing you out lately?” Then listen well. If you or someone near you is continually low in mood, or has thoughts of self-harm, please seek help from a doctor or a local crisis line right away; that, too, is an act of faith.
Pass it on: For you, which is harder, happiness or meaning? If you could choose only one, which would you choose?
Quiz

quiz.q: What is the most often cited finding of the Harvard Study of Adult Development?
o: Income is the best predictor of health and long life
The quality of close relationships is closely tied to health and happiness in later life
The more friends, the better
quiz.e: The quality of relationships matters more than the number of friends. This is a finding of long-term correlation.

quiz.q: Which statement about money and happiness is the fairest?
o: Money has nothing to do with happiness
The more money, the happier, without exception
The suffering of poverty is real and money helps; but money cannot replace meaning, and the long-term relationship is still debated
quiz.e: The Easterlin paradox and its critics are still being discussed.

quiz.q: In the Beatitudes, on whom does Jesus place the word “blessed”?
o: The poor in spirit, those who mourn, and those who hunger and thirst for righteousness
The wealthy, the healthy and the successful in their careers
Those who are never sad
quiz.e: The Beatitudes do not promise an easy life. This joy comes from a relationship with God and is no prosperity gospel.

questions.q: Why can nothing in this world truly satisfy my heart?
If I am only a brain, can I still freely love?
Is belief in God just a trick of the brain?
As AI grows smarter, what makes humans different?
